newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev ends weaker despite c.bank support.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev ends weaker despite c.bank support.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 224.50-226 per dollar at the close from 223.50-224.50 in the morning due to high foreign currency demand and despite central bank dollar sales, dealers said.
"Banks and end customers sought relatively large (foreign currency) volumes but supply was very low due to expectations of a dollar rise," a dealer said. @

Expectations of a lev fall made banks and companies square or build up forex positions after the central bank on Friday cut its main interest rate, and amid uncertainty over whether Bulgaria would win much needed International Monetary Fund funding, traders said.

The central bank sold dollars between 222.50-224 levs to end clients throughout the day but the volumes it offered were insufficient to meet demand and some companies bought the foreign currency as high as 226 levs, dealers said.
Bulgaria hopes to win a crucial $115 million second tranche of funding from the International Monetary Fund which was postponed twice since September due to the slow pace of reform.

An IMF mission due in Sofia this week or early next week is to evaluate the government's success in closing loss-making enterprises and speeding up privatisation. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
